html:
SMTO-EXE-0196 — SMTO couldn't find that fill-in field in the PDF

GUID: 007692d6-d29a-533b-b9ef-1324c9de513a
Slug: pdf-form-field-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to fill in a field that this PDF doesn't have, or the PDF has no fill-in fields at all, for example a scanned form. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the PDF's form fields before filling it in. SMTO fills a field only when its name matches exactly, and the list shows the real names.
  2. Ask SMTO to fill the form again using the field names from that list, not the labels printed next to the boxes. The label you see on the page is often different from the field's hidden name.
  3. If the list is empty, the PDF only looks like a form. Fill it in by hand in a PDF reader or get a fillable version from whoever sent it. SMTO can only fill boxes that are real fill-in fields inside the PDF.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the new filled-in PDF it created, and the values show in the right boxes when you open it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the field names you used, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PDF form filling found no supported AcroForm fields, or a requested fully qualified field name is not in the document's field map.

What this means

  • Form filling found no supported fields, or the requested fully qualified name did not match the document's form-field map. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • Form filling found no supported fields, or the requested fully qualified name did not match the document's form-field map.

How to diagnose it

  • Read current form_fields for the same revision and compare exact names and supported field types.

How to fix it

  • Call pdf.form_fields and use the exact fully qualified names it returns (case-sensitive, dot-separated for nested fields). If it returns no fields, the document has no fillable AcroForm and must be filled another way.
  • Read pdf.form_fields and use an exact fully qualified field name.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read pdf.form_fields and use an exact fully qualified field name.

How to verify the fix

  • Every requested field resolves exactly before a new filled output is created.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
